business.title: 2D-PELSA maps multidimensional target landscapes and reveals E2-GPX4 engagement associated with ferroptosis
business.description: Current methods for mapping ligand-protein interactions struggle to resolve weak yet critical binding events and conformational dynamics, particularly for pleiotropic endogenous hormones. Here, we develop a peptide-centric, dose-resolved strategy, the two-dimensional peptide-centric local stability assay (2D-PELSA), which enables highly reliable target identification and direct estimation of local binding affinities in native cellular environments. Dose-dependent information converts static proteolysis signatures into quantitative readouts of local structural remodeling at enhanced resolution, resolving direct engagement, allosteric regulation, complex remodeling, etc. Applied to 17β-estradiol (E2)-treated BT474 breast cancer cell lysates, 2D-PELSA identifies 1288 conformotypic E2-responsive peptides and 24 candidate targets enriched in unsaturated and long-chain fatty acid metabolism with micromolar EC50 values. GPX4 is identified as an E2-engaged ferroptosis regulator with an EC50 of 2.4 μM and is downregulated by micromolar E2. Orthogonal Western blot and MS-based assays validate this interaction in lysates and living cells. Integrated proteomic, lipidomic and phenotypic analyses show that chronic micromolar E2 exposure induces lipid metabolic reprogramming, lipid peroxidation and oxidative, iron-dependent cell death that is only partially rescued by ferrostatin-1 or deferoxamine. These findings establish 2D-PELSA as a versatile platform for dissecting ligand-induced structural responses and mapping target landscapes in complex biological contexts. Identifying ligand-binding proteins and determining their affinities is important but challenging in complex systems. Here, the authors develop 2D-PELSA, a peptide-centric, dose-resolved method for target identification and local affinity estimation and reveal an E2-GPX4 link to ferroptosis.

science.title: Deriving intra-constructional ambiguity in Mandarin dōu sentences: the roles of focus, topic, and speaker intention
science.description: In Mandarin Chinese, sentences featuring the adverb dōu commonly exhibit a multiplicity of interpretations. While previous studies have mainly focused on describing inter-constructional variation, the underlying mechanisms driving intra-constructional ambiguity have not been systematically explored. This study proposes a systematic and unified explanatory model to account for the derivation of different semantic patterns within dōu sentences. Building upon the tripartite quantificational structure, the proposed model attributes these multiple interpretations to the interaction between the invariant compositional core of dōu and dynamic, context-sensitive pragmatic inferences. Specifically, this study reveals that the derivation of these surface readings systematically depends on the dynamic interplay of three crucial factors: focus position, topic nature, and speaker intention. Focus position first determines the major interpretive path: scalar exhaustivity, general exhaustivity, or exclusiveness. Topic nature then distinguishes overt-topic from covert-topic readings within the general exhaustivity branch, whereas speaker intention distinguishes scalar exclusiveness from general exclusiveness within the exclusiveness branch. By providing a principled account of these divergent readings, the proposed framework suggests that inter-constructional variation can be understood as context-specific manifestations of intra-constructional ambiguity, thereby shedding new light on the syntax-semantics-pragmatics interfaces in Chinese quantification.
